chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), from his forefathers (peace be upon them) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The believer eats by the desire of his family, and the hypocrite — his family eats by his desire.'

key_terms.الْمُؤْمِنُ: The believer — one with sincere faith manifested in selfless conduct
key_terms.الْمُنَافِقُ: The hypocrite — one whose outward religious claim conceals inner selfishness
key_terms.شَهْوَة: Desire, appetite, inclination — here referring to personal food preferences within the family

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between a believer and a hypocrite in how they treat their family according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) draws a sharp moral contrast between the believer and the hypocrite in their approach to family life. The believer is selfless — he eats according to what his family desires, putting their preferences first. The hypocrite, by contrast, is self-centered — his family eats only according to his own desire, subordinating them to his will. This teaching, preserved through Imam al-Sadiq and his forefathers, reflects the Shia ethical emphasis on generosity, selflessness, and the proper fulfillment of one's obligations to one's dependants.

en.hubeali:
